title: Holidays when someone hates flying: 7 trips by train and ferry
author: Brogan
intro: If one of you won't fly, you can still go abroad. Eurostar and the overnight ferries reach cities, beaches and mountains, and the journey can be part of the holiday.
seo_title: Holidays without flying: 7 trips by train and ferry
seo_description: Paris, Amsterdam, Bruges and Cologne by Eurostar, Brittany or northern Spain by ferry: 7 holidays for when someone hates flying, with journey times.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Quickest by train:** Paris or Brussels
- **Overnight ferry:** Amsterdam or Rotterdam
- **Beach by ferry:** Brittany
- **Sunshine by ferry:** northern Spain
- **Mountains by train:** the Alps

Fear of flying is common, and some people simply prefer not to. From the UK, the Channel Tunnel and the ferries open up a surprising amount of Europe without going near an airport.

sections.heading: Seven trips at a glance
sections.text:
| Trip | How | Journey from the UK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Paris](/destinations/paris) | Eurostar from London | About 2½ hours |
| [Bruges](/destinations/bruges) | Eurostar to Brussels, then a local train | About 3½ hours |
| [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) | Eurostar, or overnight ferry from Newcastle | About 4 hours by train |
| [Cologne](/destinations/cologne) | Eurostar, change in Brussels | About 5 hours |
| [Saint-Malo](/destinations/saint-malo) | Overnight ferry from Portsmouth | One night on board |
| [Bilbao](/destinations/bilbao) | Ferry from Portsmouth | About a day and a night |
| [Annecy](/destinations/annecy) | Eurostar to Paris, then a TGV | Most of a day |

Journey times are approximate and depend on connections and the season. Check current timetables before you book, as ferry routes and frequencies change through the year.

sections.heading: By Eurostar: cities in a morning
sections.text:
Eurostar is the easiest way to go abroad without flying. You check in about an hour before, there are no liquid rules, and you arrive in the middle of the city.

- **Paris and Brussels** are both close enough for a weekend, with trains through the day.
- **Amsterdam** has direct trains, which take about four hours.
- **Bruges and Cologne** need a change in Brussels, but are still easy in a day.

Our guide to [where you can go on the Eurostar](/blog/where-can-you-go-on-the-eurostar) has more destinations and booking tips, and [Christmas markets by train from London](/blog/christmas-markets-by-train-from-london) covers the festive trips.

sections.heading: By overnight ferry: wake up abroad
sections.text:
Overnight ferries turn the journey into a mini-cruise: dinner, a cabin, and you wake up in another country.

- **Newcastle to Amsterdam** (IJmuiden) with DFDS, for a city break.
- **Hull to Rotterdam** with P&O Ferries, for the Netherlands and Belgium.
- **Portsmouth to Saint-Malo** with Brittany Ferries, for the walled town and the beaches of Brittany.

Tip: book a cabin with a window if you can, and arrive at the port early. Driving off a ferry with your own car means you can carry as much luggage as you like, which makes a ferry holiday easier than flying in some ways.

sections.heading: Sun without a plane: northern Spain
sections.text:
If someone wants a beach and someone else won't fly, Brittany Ferries' sailings from Portsmouth and Plymouth to Bilbao and Santander are the answer. You spend a night or two at sea, then drive off into northern Spain.

[Bilbao](/destinations/bilbao) has the Guggenheim and great food, [San Sebastián](/destinations/san-sebastian) has one of the best city beaches in Europe, and [Asturias](/destinations/asturias) has green mountains and quiet coves. It's not guaranteed sun like the Canaries, but summer is warm and pleasant.

Watch out: the Bay of Biscay can be rough, especially outside summer. If anyone's prone to seasickness, choose a summer crossing and a cabin in the middle of the ship.

sections.heading: Driving: through the tunnel
sections.text:
If you'd rather take your own car, LeShuttle carries cars through the Channel Tunnel from Folkestone to Calais in about 35 minutes. From Calais, you can be in Bruges in about an hour and a half, Paris in about three hours, or keep going south for a road trip.

- **No luggage limits:** pack the car as full as you like.
- **Flexible:** many tickets let you travel on an earlier or later train if you arrive early or late.
- **Road trips:** our [road trips](/destinations/road-trips) page has routes across Europe that start well from the Channel ports.

The short ferry crossings from Dover to Calais and Dunkirk are an alternative, and some people prefer the sea air to the tunnel.

sections.heading: Making it work for everyone
sections.text:
When one of you won't fly, it's worth agreeing early what each person wants most. A mountain lover and a city lover can both be happy in the Alps by train; a beach lover and a non-flyer can meet in Brittany or northern Spain.

- **Make the journey part of the trip:** a good lunch on the train or a cabin on the ferry.
- **Go further, less often:** one longer trip by train can beat two short ones by plane.
- **Split the travel:** take the train out and the ferry back for variety.

Our post on [holidays when everyone wants something different](/blog/when-everyone-wants-a-different-holiday) has more ideas for compromises, and [how to agree on a holiday as a family](/blog/how-to-agree-on-a-holiday-as-a-family) covers the conversation itself.

sections.heading: More ideas
sections.text: Our [train holidays](/destinations/train-holidays) page has the most scenic rail journeys in Europe and beyond, many of which start with a Eurostar. If you're still undecided, add a few of these trips to [somewhere.party](/), give everyone points to spend, and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Where can you go on holiday from the UK without flying?
faqs.answer: France, Belgium and the Netherlands are easiest by Eurostar, and ferries reach Brittany, northern Spain and the Netherlands. With connections, you can reach most of Western Europe by train.

faqs.question: How long does the Eurostar take to Paris?
faqs.answer: About two and a half hours from London St Pancras to Paris Gare du Nord on the fastest trains.

faqs.question: Can you get to Spain without flying?
faqs.answer: Yes. Brittany Ferries sails from Portsmouth and Plymouth to Bilbao and Santander, or you can take Eurostar to Paris and a train south.

faqs.question: Is there an overnight ferry to Amsterdam?
faqs.answer: Yes. DFDS sails overnight from Newcastle to IJmuiden, near Amsterdam, and P&O Ferries sails overnight from Hull to Rotterdam.
